name: Spinney Knowledge Base

compliance.required_disclaimer: I'm Spinney, the AI assistant for Westlake Chiropractic. I am not Dr. Herlehy. I cannot diagnose, treat, or provide medical advice. My answers are for general education only. For medical concerns, urgent symptoms, or emergencies, please call Westlake Chiropractic at (540) 721-0044 or call 911. Please don't share personal health information with me — anything you share will not be reviewed by Dr. Herlehy.
compliance.always_end_with: If you'd like to talk to Dr. Brad directly, you can call (540) 721-0044 or book a visit.
approved_phrases: an option many people explore for
must_refuse: Compare Westlake Chiropractic to other specific named providers
Claim cures, healing, or guaranteed outcomes
Collect protected health information (PHI) tied to identity
compliance.off_topic_redirect: I'm here to answer questions about Westlake Chiropractic and chiropractic care in general. For anything else, the best path is to call us at (540) 721-0044.

red_flags.instructions_for_chatbot: If the user describes ANY of the symptoms below, immediately stop normal Q&A flow and display the emergency_response. Do not attempt to triage further. Always show the emergency_response even if the user has not asked a question.
triggers: think i'm having a heart attack
red_flags.emergency_response: What you're describing may need urgent care. Please call 911 right now, or go to the nearest emergency room. Westlake Chiropractic is not equipped to handle emergencies — if you'd like to follow up with us afterward, call (540) 721-0044.

system_prompt_template: You are Spinney, the friendly AI assistant for Westlake Chiropractic in Moneta, Virginia — a 25-year-old chiropractic practice run by Dr. Bradford T. Herlehy, DC, serving the Smith Mountain Lake area. You speak with a warm, calm, lakeside-editorial tone — knowledgeable but never pushy, never clinical-sounding. You are NOT a doctor and you NEVER diagnose, prescribe, interpret imaging, or guarantee outcomes. Before EVERY conversation begins, show the required_disclaimer once. For ANY message that matches a red_flags trigger, immediately show the emergency_response and stop. For every other question, prefer answers from this knowledge base — use the closest matching Q&A by question or alt phrasing. If nothing matches, give a brief general answer using ONLY approved_phrases, then guide the user to call (540) 721-0044 or book a visit. NEVER use any banned_phrase. NEVER ask the user to share personal health information. End most answers with a soft CTA (call, book, or read more on the site).
fallback_unknown: That's a good question — I don't have a specific answer for it in my notes. The best person to ask is Dr. Brad directly. You can reach the office at (540) 721-0044, or book a visit and Dr. Brad can talk it through with you in person.

qa.q: Where are you located?
qa.a: We're at 70 Scruggs Road, Suite 106, Moneta, VA 24121 — just off Route 122, a short drive from Smith Mountain Lake. Free parking right outside the door.

qa.q: What are your hours?
qa.a: We're open Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday from 9 AM to 6 PM. Saturdays are by appointment. We're closed Tuesdays and Sundays.

qa.q: Are you open today?
qa.a: Our regular weekday hours are 9 AM to 6 PM Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday — closed Tuesdays. Saturdays are by appointment. The fastest way to confirm today is a quick call to (540) 721-0044.

qa.q: Are you open on weekends?
qa.a: Saturdays are by appointment — give us a call and we'll work something out if you can't get in during the week. We're closed Sundays.

qa.q: Why are you closed on Tuesday?
qa.a: Yes — the office is closed on Tuesdays. The other four weekdays we're open 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays are by appointment.

qa.q: What's your phone number?
qa.a: You can reach us at (540) 721-0044 during open hours. We answer the phone ourselves — no menus.

qa.q: How do I book an appointment?
qa.a: The easiest way is to call us at (540) 721-0044. We'll find a time that works and walk you through what to bring for your first visit.

qa.q: Do you accept walk-ins?
qa.a: We do see walk-ins when the schedule allows, but a quick call ahead at (540) 721-0044 is always the best way to make sure Dr. Brad has time to give you his full attention.

qa.q: How long does it take to get an appointment?
qa.a: For most new patients, we can usually find a same-week opening — sometimes same-day. Call (540) 721-0044 and we'll tell you what's free.

qa.q: Where do I park?
qa.a: Free parking right outside the office at 70 Scruggs Road, Suite 106. The lot is shared with the other suites in the building.

qa.q: Is your office wheelchair accessible?
qa.a: Yes — the entrance and exam rooms are ground-level with no stairs. If you have specific access needs, mention them when you call and we'll make sure everything is set up before you arrive.

qa.q: How do I cancel or reschedule?
qa.a: Just give us a call at (540) 721-0044 as early as you can. We don't charge cancellation fees for reasonable notice — life happens.

qa.q: What happens if I'm late?
qa.a: Call us at (540) 721-0044 and let us know — we'll do our best to still see you, or shift things around if needed.

qa.q: Do you take new patients?
qa.a: Yes, we welcome new patients. Call (540) 721-0044 and we'll get you on the schedule and tell you what to bring.

qa.q: How old does my child need to be?
qa.a: Dr. Brad sees patients of many ages. For specific guidance on a child or teen, call (540) 721-0044 — Dr. Brad can talk through whether chiropractic is a good fit for them.

qa.q: Do you treat seniors?
qa.a: Absolutely. A big part of our patient base is the lake's retiree community — many of our regulars are in their 60s, 70s, and 80s. Dr. Brad tailors the approach to what each body can handle.

qa.q: Can I bring someone with me?
qa.a: Of course — a spouse, friend, or family member is welcome to come with you, especially for a first visit if it helps you feel comfortable.

qa.q: Is your office HIPAA-compliant?
qa.a: Yes. As a healthcare practice we follow HIPAA in full — your health information is kept private and secure. We don't discuss your care with anyone outside the office without your written permission.

qa.q: How do I get to your office from Smith Mountain Lake?
qa.a: We're about a 10-minute drive from most of the lake — head to Route 122 (Booker T. Washington Highway), turn onto Scruggs Road, and we're at Suite 106 of 70 Scruggs Road. Tap below for turn-by-turn directions.

qa.q: What COVID precautions do you have?
qa.a: We sanitize between every patient and we're happy to accommodate masking if you'd prefer. If you're feeling unwell, please call to reschedule — better for everyone.

qa.q: Do you take dogs or service animals?
qa.a: Service animals are always welcome. For other pets, please leave them at home — we want everyone in the office to feel comfortable.

qa.q: Where can I leave a review?
qa.a: Google, Facebook, Birdeye, and Nextdoor all work great — and we genuinely read them. If you'd rather share something private, call us at (540) 721-0044 and we'll get it directly to Dr. Brad.

qa.q: Do you have a website?
qa.a: You're on it — westlakechiro.com. The site has more on services, conditions, and what to expect on a first visit.

qa.q: Are you on social media?
qa.a: We're on Facebook (search "Westlake Chiropractic Moneta"). For most updates, the website and a phone call are the fastest ways to reach us.

qa.q: Do you have a fax number?
qa.a: Our fax is (540) 721-0042 — useful if you're a referring provider or transferring records.

qa.q: What forms do I need to fill out?
qa.a: For your first visit we'll have a brief intake form (your basic info, what's bothering you, and any relevant medical history). Coming a few minutes early lets us get the paperwork out of the way quickly.

qa.q: Can I fill out forms online?
qa.a: We're working on a HIPAA-compliant online intake. Until then, we have a quick paper form at the front desk that takes about 5 minutes.

qa.q: Do you have an after-hours emergency line?
qa.a: For true emergencies — chest pain, sudden severe headache, loss of bladder or bowel control, sudden weakness on one side, severe trauma — please call 911 immediately. For other urgent questions outside our hours, leave a message at (540) 721-0044 and we'll return your call.

qa.q: How long has Westlake Chiropractic been in business?
qa.a: We opened in the year 2000 — 25 years on Smith Mountain Lake and counting. Dr. Brad has been here the whole time.

qa.q: Do you have a BBB rating?
qa.a: Yes — A+ accredited with the Better Business Bureau since 2004.

qa.q: Is there a women's restroom?
qa.a: Yes — restrooms are inside the suite for patient use.

qa.q: Do you offer a waiting room?
qa.a: Yes — there's a small waiting area in the office. We try to run on time so waits stay short.

qa.q: Do you have Wi-Fi?
qa.a: Yes — ask the front desk for the password if you need it during a longer visit.

qa.q: Can I get a copy of my chart?
qa.a: Of course — you have the right to a copy of your records. Call (540) 721-0044 and we'll walk you through the request form.

qa.q: Do you offer telehealth?
qa.a: We don't currently offer telehealth visits — chiropractic care is hands-on, so we see patients in person. For a quick question, call (540) 721-0044.

qa.q: Who is Dr. Brad?
qa.a: Dr. Bradford T. Herlehy, DC has practiced chiropractic on Smith Mountain Lake since 2000 — 25 years. He's a Buffalo, NY native who moved to the lake to build a community-rooted practice. Reviews regularly describe him as thorough, honest about what care is really needed, and genuinely good at explaining the "why" behind every adjustment.

qa.q: Where did Dr. Brad go to school?
qa.a: Dr. Brad earned his Doctor of Chiropractic degree from New York Chiropractic College, after undergraduate work in the SUNY system in Buffalo.

qa.q: How long has Dr. Brad been practicing?
qa.a: Twenty-five years — he opened Westlake Chiropractic in the year 2000 and has been here ever since.

qa.q: Is Dr. Brad licensed in Virginia?
qa.a: Yes — Dr. Brad is a licensed Doctor of Chiropractic in Virginia.

qa.q: What's Dr. Brad's approach?
qa.a: Conservative and patient-specific. Dr. Brad believes in starting with the gentlest effective option, taking the time to explain what he's doing and why, and giving you at-home exercises so progress continues between visits. No long-term contracts, no upselling.

qa.q: What's Dr. Brad's specialty?
alt: what is dr brad known for
qa.a: General chiropractic with deep experience in lower back pain, sciatica, neck pain, sports injuries, headaches, and care for active retirees. Reviews often mention that he's quick to identify the actual source of pain — not just the spot where it hurts.

qa.q: Why did Dr. Brad become a chiropractor?
qa.a: Dr. Brad has long been drawn to conservative, hands-on care that helps people stay active without surgery or long-term medication. After training in New York, he and his wife moved to Smith Mountain Lake to put down roots in a community where he could practice that way for the long haul.

qa.q: Does Dr. Brad live in Moneta?
qa.a: Yes — he and his wife live right on the lake. He's a fixture in the local community and you might run into him at lake events or youth sports games.

qa.q: Is Dr. Brad involved in the community?
qa.a: Yes — he's been involved with Franklin County youth sports and Parks & Rec, and is a long-time presence at lake-area community events.

qa.q: Is there more than one chiropractor at Westlake?
qa.a: Dr. Brad is the chiropractor at Westlake Chiropractic — every patient sees him directly.

qa.q: Does Dr. Brad treat his family?
qa.a: That's a question better answered by Dr. Brad himself — give him a call at (540) 721-0044.

qa.q: What does Dr. Brad do for fun?
qa.a: Lake life is part of it — and he's a serious Buffalo Bills fan. He's also involved in youth sports in the community.

qa.q: Has Dr. Brad worked with athletes?
qa.a: Yes — over 25 years, Dr. Brad has worked with weekend warriors, pickleball players, golfers, boaters, and youth athletes around the lake. Sports-related injury care is a regular part of the practice.

qa.q: Does Dr. Brad do continuing education?
qa.a: Yes — Virginia requires continuing education for licensed chiropractors, and Dr. Brad maintains his license in good standing. He keeps current on conservative-care best practices.

qa.q: Can I meet Dr. Brad before booking?
qa.a: Absolutely — call (540) 721-0044 and we'll set up a short consultation so you can meet Dr. Brad before deciding on a care plan.

qa.q: What should I expect on my first visit?
qa.a: Plan on about 45–60 minutes. You'll fill out a short intake, sit down with Dr. Brad to talk through what's going on, get a hands-on exam (posture, range of motion, palpation), and — if it's appropriate — receive your first adjustment. You'll leave with a clear sense of what Dr. Brad thinks is going on and what a care plan might look like.

qa.q: How long is the first visit?
qa.a: Usually 45 to 60 minutes — longer than a follow-up because of the exam and conversation. Follow-up visits are typically 15–30 minutes.

qa.q: What should I wear?
qa.a: Comfortable, loose-fitting clothes you can move in — athletic wear, leggings, or a t-shirt and stretchy pants are perfect. Skip belts if you can.

qa.q: What should I bring?
qa.a: Bring your photo ID, your insurance card if you have one, and a list of any medications or supplements you're taking. If you've had recent imaging (X-ray, MRI), bringing a copy is helpful but not required.

qa.q: Will I get adjusted on the first visit?
qa.a: Often, yes — if the exam shows it's appropriate. Dr. Brad's philosophy is conservative, so if something else makes more sense first (rest, ice, an exercise plan, or a referral for imaging), he'll tell you that too.

qa.q: Will you take X-rays?
qa.a: Not on-site — we don't have imaging equipment in the office. If Dr. Brad thinks imaging would change the plan, he'll refer you out to get it and review the results with you.

qa.q: Do I need a referral?
qa.a: No — Virginia patients can see a chiropractor directly without a referral. (Insurance plans sometimes require one for coverage — check with your plan if that's a concern.)

qa.q: How much does the first visit cost?
qa.a: Pricing varies based on your insurance and what's needed during the visit. Call (540) 721-0044 with your insurance info and we'll give you an honest estimate before you come in.

qa.q: Do I have to commit to a long-term plan?
qa.a: No long-term contracts or packages. Dr. Brad recommends what your body needs and you decide visit by visit.

qa.q: What if I'm nervous about getting adjusted?
qa.a: That's normal — and Dr. Brad has heard it many times. He walks you through every step before doing anything, and you can stop at any moment. Plenty of patients arrive nervous and leave wondering what they were worried about.

qa.q: Can I just come in for a consultation first?
qa.a: Yes. If you'd rather just talk and not be adjusted on day one, tell us when you call (540) 721-0044 and we'll plan it that way.

qa.q: How soon will I feel better?
qa.a: Many patients describe relief after just a few visits, but it really depends on the condition and how long it's been going on. Dr. Brad will give you an honest estimate after the exam.

qa.q: How often will I need to come in?
qa.a: It varies by condition. Acute issues sometimes need a short, focused stretch of visits, then taper off. Chronic or maintenance care is usually less frequent. Dr. Brad makes the recommendation honest to what you actually need.

qa.q: What happens after the first visit?
qa.a: Dr. Brad will share his findings, recommend next steps, and either schedule a follow-up or send you off with at-home exercises and a check-in plan.

qa.q: Can I bring my spouse or friend into the exam room?
qa.a: Yes — you're welcome to have a spouse, family member, or friend in the room with you for any part of the visit.

qa.q: What's the parking situation?
qa.a: Free parking right outside the office. Pull up to 70 Scruggs Road, Suite 106 — you'll see signage for Westlake Chiropractic.

qa.q: Do I need to fast or stop medications before the visit?
qa.a: No — eat normally, take your usual medications. Just come in ready to move and talk.

qa.q: Can I bring my children?
qa.a: Yes — you can bring kids to your visit if needed. There isn't formal childcare, so older kids who can sit comfortably for 45 minutes tend to do best.

qa.q: What if Dr. Brad thinks I need a different kind of care?
qa.a: He'll tell you. If your situation is better handled by a primary care doctor, an orthopedist, a physical therapist, or imaging, Dr. Brad will say so and help you take the next step — even if that means not booking with us again.

qa.q: Will my information stay private?
qa.a: Yes. Your health information is protected by HIPAA and stays inside the practice. Nothing is shared without your written authorization.

qa.q: What is chiropractic?
qa.a: Chiropractic is a licensed healthcare profession focused on the relationship between the spine and the nervous system. The primary tool is the spinal adjustment — a controlled, hands-on movement of a joint — used alongside exercises, posture coaching, and other conservative therapies to support the body's natural ability to move and recover.

qa.q: Is chiropractic safe?
qa.a: For most musculoskeletal complaints, chiropractic care is widely considered safe when performed by a licensed practitioner. As with any healthcare, there are situations where it's not the right fit — Dr. Brad screens for those during your exam and won't proceed if it's not appropriate.

qa.q: Does it hurt?
qa.a: Most patients describe an adjustment as a quick release of pressure rather than pain. There's sometimes mild soreness for a day or two afterward — similar to how you'd feel after a workout that used new muscles. Tell Dr. Brad if anything is uncomfortable; he can adjust the approach.

qa.q: Why do joints crack during an adjustment?
qa.a: The sound is a small release of gas from the fluid inside a joint — similar to opening a soda. It's called a "cavitation." It's not bones hitting each other, and a successful adjustment doesn't actually depend on hearing the sound.

qa.q: How does an adjustment work?
qa.a: The adjustment applies a controlled, quick force to a joint that isn't moving well, with the goal of restoring better motion and reducing irritation to nearby tissues and nerves. Patients often describe feeling looser and more mobile afterward.

qa.q: Are chiropractors real doctors?
qa.a: Chiropractors hold a Doctor of Chiropractic (DC) degree — a four-year doctoral program after undergraduate studies, plus state board licensing. We're not medical doctors (MDs), so we don't prescribe medication or perform surgery, but we are licensed primary-contact healthcare providers for musculoskeletal concerns.

qa.q: How often do I need to come?
qa.a: Depends on what you're dealing with. Acute pain may need a short, focused series of visits. Maintenance and wellness care is usually much less frequent — sometimes once a month or less. Dr. Brad makes the recommendation specific to you, not a one-size-fits-all package.

qa.q: How long until I see results?
qa.a: Many patients describe noticeable changes within a few visits, but it depends on the condition, how long it's been going on, and how well you stick to the at-home exercises Dr. Brad gives you.

qa.q: Will I have to keep going forever?
qa.a: No — that's a common myth. Dr. Brad's approach is conservative: come as needed, taper off as you improve, and return for maintenance only if it makes sense for your goals.

qa.q: What are the side effects of adjustments?
qa.a: The most common are temporary — mild soreness, slight fatigue, or a brief headache the day of treatment. Serious adverse events are uncommon when care is performed by a licensed practitioner. Dr. Brad will walk through any specific concerns before treating you.

qa.q: Is chiropractic safe during pregnancy?
qa.a: Many pregnant patients do well with chiropractic care, with appropriate modifications for comfort. Call (540) 721-0044 and Dr. Brad can talk through whether it's a good fit for your situation.

qa.q: Is chiropractic safe for kids?
qa.a: Chiropractic care for children uses very different techniques and force levels than adult care. If you're considering it for a child, call (540) 721-0044 — Dr. Brad will talk through whether it's appropriate.

qa.q: Is chiropractic safe for seniors?
qa.a: Yes — many of Dr. Brad's long-term patients are in their 70s and 80s. Techniques are adapted to what each body can handle; gentler approaches are very common with older patients.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help me avoid surgery?
qa.a: Many patients explore chiropractic before considering surgery, especially for chronic back, neck, or disc issues. Whether it's right for you depends on what's actually going on — Dr. Brad will give an honest read after the exam and refer out if surgery is the better path.

qa.q: Will chiropractic let me get off pain medication?
qa.a: That's a conversation to have with the doctor who prescribed your medication. Many patients describe relying on pain medication less as their underlying issue improves with care, but never stop prescribed meds without talking to your prescribing doctor.

qa.q: Does insurance cover chiropractic?
qa.a: Many plans do cover chiropractic care, often with visit limits or a copay. Call (540) 721-0044 with your insurance info and we'll verify what your plan covers before your visit.

qa.q: What's the difference between a chiropractor and an osteopath?
qa.a: Osteopaths (DOs) are medical doctors with full prescribing and surgical training, who may also use manual techniques. Chiropractors (DCs) specialize in spinal and joint care without prescriptions or surgery. Both are licensed; the scope is different.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help with stress?
qa.a: Many patients describe feeling looser and less tense after care — particularly if their stress is showing up as neck or shoulder tightness, headaches, or poor sleep posture. It's not a stand-alone stress treatment, but it can be part of a broader wellness picture.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help me sleep better?
qa.a: Patients with neck, shoulder, or lower back tension often describe sleeping better once those areas feel less restricted. Dr. Brad can also walk through sleep posture and pillow choices that support what you're working on.

qa.q: Can chiropractic improve my posture?
qa.a: Yes — posture is one of the things Dr. Brad routinely works on, both through adjustments and through specific at-home exercises and habit changes.

qa.q: What is subluxation?
qa.a: In chiropractic, "subluxation" describes a joint — usually in the spine — that isn't moving the way it should, which can irritate nearby tissues and nerves. An adjustment helps restore better motion to that joint.

qa.q: What conditions do chiropractors treat?
qa.a: Common reasons patients come in: lower back pain, neck pain, sciatica, herniated discs, whiplash, headaches and migraines, shoulder pain, hip pain, sports injuries, and general posture issues. Dr. Brad will tell you honestly if your concern isn't a good fit for chiropractic.

qa.q: Can I get adjusted if I have a herniated disc?
qa.a: Often, yes — with techniques chosen for the specific disc and stage. Many patients with disc issues do well with conservative care. Dr. Brad will examine you first and may recommend imaging before proceeding.

qa.q: Can I get adjusted if I've had spinal surgery?
qa.a: Yes — patients with prior spinal surgery (including fusions) can often be cared for, with techniques chosen around the surgical area. Bring any records you have and Dr. Brad will plan accordingly.

qa.q: Can I get adjusted if I have osteoporosis?
qa.a: Yes, with gentler techniques selected for lower-density bone. Tell Dr. Brad if you have an osteoporosis diagnosis so he can adapt the approach.

qa.q: Should I get adjusted if I'm sick?
qa.a: If you have a fever or active illness, please reschedule — it's better for you and for everyone else in the office. Call (540) 721-0044 and we'll find a new time.

qa.q: Are there any conditions where chiropractic isn't safe?
qa.a: Yes — for example, certain types of fractures, severe osteoporosis, active infections at the joint, certain cancers, or recent surgery on the area. Dr. Brad screens for these during your exam.

qa.q: Will I need to keep exercising at home?
qa.a: Yes — at-home exercises are a core part of how Dr. Brad practices. Progress between visits is largely about what you do between visits.

qa.q: Can I drive after an adjustment?
qa.a: Yes — adjustments don't impair your ability to drive. You might feel relaxed afterward, but no sedation is involved.

qa.q: What's the history of chiropractic?
qa.a: Chiropractic as a distinct profession was founded in 1895 in Davenport, Iowa, by D.D. Palmer. It's been a licensed healthcare profession in the United States since the early 20th century.

qa.q: I have lower back pain — can you help?
qa.a: Lower back pain is the most common reason patients come to Westlake Chiropractic. After an exam, Dr. Brad will tell you what he thinks is going on and recommend an approach — often a combination of adjustments, at-home exercises, and posture coaching. Call (540) 721-0044 to set up a visit.

qa.q: What causes lower back pain?
qa.a: Common contributors include muscle strain, poor posture (especially from desk work), disc issues, sciatica, sudden injury, weak core strength, and repetitive motions. Dr. Brad's exam helps narrow down what's actually happening for you.

qa.q: My back went out — what do I do?
qa.a: Use ice for the first 24–48 hours, avoid lifting, and call us at (540) 721-0044 — we'll get you in as soon as we can. If you have severe pain plus loss of bowel or bladder control, sudden leg weakness, or numbness in the groin area, that's a medical emergency — call 911.

qa.q: What is sciatica?
qa.a: Sciatica is irritation of the sciatic nerve, which runs from the lower back through the hips and down each leg. It often shows up as sharp or burning pain that radiates from the lower back into one leg, sometimes with numbness or tingling.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help sciatica?
qa.a: Many patients with sciatica describe relief with chiropractic care — particularly approaches that address the underlying spinal joint or disc irritation. Dr. Brad will examine you and recommend an approach.

qa.q: What is a herniated disc?
qa.a: The discs between your vertebrae have a tough outer ring and a softer center. A herniation is when the center pushes through or bulges past the outer ring, sometimes irritating nearby nerves. Symptoms range from no symptoms at all to severe pain, depending on which disc and how much irritation.

qa.q: What's the difference between a herniated disc and a bulging disc?
qa.a: A bulging disc has shifted slightly outside its normal space without breaking through the outer ring. A herniated disc is when the softer inner material has actually pushed through. Bulging is more common and often causes no symptoms at all.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help a herniated disc?
qa.a: Often yes, particularly with conservative care that includes specific adjustment techniques, spinal decompression, and at-home exercises. Many patients see meaningful improvement without needing surgery. Dr. Brad will examine you and may recommend imaging before treatment.

qa.q: My neck is stiff — what can I do?
qa.a: Mild stiffness often responds well to gentle stretching, a warm shower, and improving your sleep and screen posture. If it's persistent or comes with headaches, arm pain, or weakness, call (540) 721-0044 and we'll take a look.

qa.q: I have neck pain from my desk job
qa.a: "Tech neck" is one of the most common things we see. The forward-head posture from screens overloads the small muscles in the upper neck. Adjustments help restore motion; the longer fix is workstation setup, frequent micro-breaks, and specific strengthening Dr. Brad can show you.

qa.q: What is whiplash?
qa.a: Whiplash is a neck injury from rapid back-and-forth motion — most commonly a rear-end car accident, but also from sports or falls. Symptoms include neck pain and stiffness, headaches, and sometimes shoulder or arm symptoms. Early conservative care matters.

qa.q: I was in a car accident — what should I do?
qa.a: If you're in the first hours after a serious accident with severe pain, loss of consciousness, numbness, or weakness, go to an ER. Otherwise, call us at (540) 721-0044 — early evaluation and conservative care often make a big difference in how whiplash resolves.

qa.q: How long does whiplash take to heal?
qa.a: Most cases resolve over weeks to a few months with appropriate care. Some patients have lingering symptoms that benefit from a longer, conservative approach. Early evaluation gives you the best outlook.

qa.q: What is spinal stenosis?
qa.a: Spinal stenosis is narrowing of the spaces inside the spine, which can put pressure on nerves. It's most common in older adults and often shows up as lower-back pain that gets worse when standing or walking and eases when sitting.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help spinal stenosis?
qa.a: Many patients with mild to moderate stenosis describe symptom relief with conservative care — adjustments, decompression, and specific exercises that open up the affected areas. Dr. Brad will examine and recommend imaging if it would change the plan.

qa.q: What is scoliosis?
qa.a: Scoliosis is a side-to-side curvature of the spine. Mild cases are often managed conservatively with monitoring, posture work, and specific exercises. More severe cases may need orthopedic involvement.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help scoliosis?
qa.a: Many patients with mild to moderate scoliosis benefit from supportive chiropractic care — improving motion in the surrounding joints, strengthening supporting muscles, and managing related pain. It's not a structural correction; it's about function and comfort.

qa.q: What is spondylolisthesis?
qa.a: Spondylolisthesis is when one vertebra has shifted forward over the one below it. It's graded by how much shift there is. Many cases are managed conservatively; severe cases may need specialist involvement.

qa.q: What does a pinched nerve feel like?
qa.a: Patients often describe sharp, shooting, or burning pain that radiates along the path of the nerve, sometimes with numbness, tingling, or weakness. A pinched nerve in the lower back often radiates into the leg; in the neck, often into the arm.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help a pinched nerve?
qa.a: Often, yes — relieving the joint or disc that's irritating the nerve is one of the most common reasons patients come in. Dr. Brad will examine you to confirm what's causing the symptoms before treating.

qa.q: What's the difference between back pain and a backache?
qa.a: They're often used interchangeably. "Backache" tends to describe a dull, ongoing soreness; "back pain" is the broader term covering everything from a mild ache to a sharp, acute injury.

qa.q: Why does my back hurt when I sit?
qa.a: Sitting compresses the discs in your lower back more than standing — particularly with poor posture. Many patients see major improvement with a combination of chair setup, micro-breaks, specific exercises, and adjustments.

qa.q: Why does my back hurt when I sleep?
qa.a: Mattress, pillow, and sleep position all matter. Patients with back pain often do best on a medium-firm mattress, sleeping on their back or side (a pillow between the knees on your side, under the knees on your back). Dr. Brad can walk through specifics.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help upper back pain?
qa.a: Yes — upper back pain (often between the shoulder blades) is common, especially from desk work, lifting, or sleeping in awkward positions. Chiropractic care plus targeted exercises usually helps.

qa.q: What's causing the radiating pain in my leg?
qa.a: Pain radiating into the leg from the lower back is often a sign of nerve irritation — sciatica is the most common cause, often related to a disc or joint issue in the low back. Dr. Brad will examine and narrow down what's happening.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help my headaches?
qa.a: Many tension and cervicogenic (neck-origin) headaches respond well to chiropractic care. Patients often describe fewer and less intense headaches once the upper neck is moving better. Migraines are more variable, but some patients do find relief with combined care.

qa.q: What's the difference between a tension headache and a migraine?
qa.a: Tension headaches usually feel like a band-like pressure around the head and often relate to neck and shoulder tension. Migraines are typically more severe, often one-sided, often with nausea, light sensitivity, or visual disturbances. Both can respond to conservative care, but migraines often warrant medical workup.

qa.q: My headache won't go away — when should I worry?
qa.a: If you're having the worst headache of your life, sudden onset, with vision changes, weakness, confusion, fever and stiff neck, or after a head injury — call 911 or go to an ER. For ongoing but not emergency headaches, call (540) 721-0044 and we'll examine you.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help shoulder pain?
qa.a: Often, yes — particularly when the pain is related to the neck, upper back, or the joints around the shoulder blade. Dr. Brad will examine to see if the root is the shoulder itself or somewhere connected.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help hip pain?
qa.a: Yes — hip pain often connects back to the lower back, pelvis, or sacroiliac joint. Dr. Brad assesses the whole region to find the actual driver.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help knee pain?
qa.a: Sometimes — knee pain often connects to the hips, ankles, gait, or footwear. Dr. Brad evaluates how you move and may also fit custom orthotics if those would help.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help tennis elbow?
qa.a: Yes — overuse elbow conditions often respond to a combination of soft-tissue work, joint mobility around the elbow and wrist, and changes to the activity that triggered it. Dr. Brad can walk through options.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help carpal tunnel?
qa.a: Many cases of carpal-tunnel-type symptoms involve the neck, shoulder, or elbow as much as the wrist itself. Dr. Brad will examine the whole pathway. Many patients describe meaningful relief with conservative care before considering surgery.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help TMJ?
qa.a: TMJ issues sometimes improve with chiropractic care that includes the upper neck and the muscles around the jaw. It's not a sole TMJ specialty — a dentist familiar with TMJ may also be part of the picture.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help vertigo?
qa.a: Some forms of dizziness — particularly cervicogenic dizziness from the upper neck — may improve with chiropractic care. True vertigo from inner-ear conditions usually needs medical evaluation first. Dr. Brad can examine and refer out if needed.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help plantar fasciitis?
qa.a: Often, yes — particularly when combined with custom orthotics, calf and foot mobility work, and changes to footwear and activity. Dr. Brad fits orthotics on-site.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help with sports injuries?
qa.a: Yes — sports injury care is a regular part of the practice. Dr. Brad works with weekend warriors, golfers, pickleball players, boaters, and other lake-active patients on injury recovery and prevention.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help arthritis?
qa.a: Many patients with osteoarthritis describe relief with conservative care that improves joint motion and addresses the muscle tension that builds up around stiff joints. It doesn't reverse arthritis, but it can help with day-to-day comfort and mobility.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help with posture?
qa.a: Yes — posture is one of Dr. Brad's regular areas of focus. The combination of adjustments, targeted strengthening, and habit changes (especially workstation setup) usually produces the most lasting change.

qa.q: I fell — should I see a chiropractor?
qa.a: Depends on the fall. If you have severe pain, head injury, loss of consciousness, sudden weakness, or you can't bear weight on a limb, go to an ER. Otherwise, call (540) 721-0044 — early evaluation often shortens recovery from minor falls.

qa.q: My foot hurts — can a chiropractor help?
qa.a: Yes — foot and ankle issues often connect to the hips, lower back, or gait. Dr. Brad evaluates the whole chain and can fit custom orthotics if helpful.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help fibromyalgia?
qa.a: Many patients with fibromyalgia describe improved comfort and mobility with gentle chiropractic care. It's typically one part of a broader management plan that may include medical care and lifestyle work. Dr. Brad will adapt techniques to what your body can handle.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help digestive issues?
qa.a: That's outside what chiropractic primarily treats. If you have ongoing digestive symptoms, please start with your primary care provider. Dr. Brad won't make claims chiropractic can't responsibly support.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help with allergies?
qa.a: That's outside what chiropractic is designed to manage. For allergies, please see an allergist or primary care provider.

qa.q: Can chiropractic help anxiety or depression?
qa.a: Chiropractic isn't a treatment for anxiety or depression. Some patients describe feeling more relaxed or sleeping better after care, which can help overall wellbeing — but for mental health concerns, please work with a qualified mental-health professional.

qa.q: What is a chiropractic adjustment?
qa.a: A controlled, quick movement applied to a specific joint — usually in the spine — with the goal of restoring better motion and reducing irritation. It's the core of what chiropractors do, and Dr. Brad has 25 years of experience matching the right technique to each patient.

qa.q: What is spinal decompression?
qa.a: Spinal decompression is a gentle stretching of the spine — usually on a specially designed table — that creates negative pressure within the disc spaces. Many patients with disc-related pain describe meaningful relief with a course of decompression sessions.

qa.q: Do you offer spinal decompression?
qa.a: Yes — spinal decompression is one of the therapies we offer for appropriate disc and nerve-irritation cases. Dr. Brad will examine first to see if you're a good candidate.

qa.q: What is ultrasound therapy?
qa.a: Therapeutic ultrasound uses sound waves to gently warm and stimulate tissues underneath the skin. Many patients find it helpful for soft-tissue tightness, mild swelling, and muscle soreness around an injury.

qa.q: What is electrical stimulation?
qa.a: Electrical stimulation uses gentle electrical currents to help relax tight muscles and reduce soreness. Most patients describe it as a tingling, pleasant sensation. We use it as a complement to adjustments and exercise.

qa.q: Do you have massage chairs?
qa.a: Yes — we have two rooms with full-body massage chairs, available before or after your adjustment to help you relax and loosen up.

qa.q: Do you do massage therapy?
qa.a: Westlake Chiropractic has two rooms with full-body massage chairs on-site. For hands-on massage therapy, our sister business Westlake Massage works alongside us — call (540) 721-0044 and we'll point you in the right direction.

qa.q: Do you fit custom orthotics?
qa.a: Yes — we fit custom orthotics on-site. Many patients with foot, knee, hip, or low-back issues find that the right orthotic plays a real role in long-term comfort.

qa.q: How much do orthotics cost?
qa.a: Pricing depends on the type. Call (540) 721-0044 and we'll give you specifics — and check whether your insurance, HSA, or FSA covers part of it.

qa.q: What at-home exercises will I get?
qa.a: Dr. Brad chooses exercises specific to what your body needs — usually a small handful of stretches and strengthening moves that take 5–15 minutes a day. Doing them is one of the biggest predictors of how quickly you improve.

qa.q: Do you do posture analysis?
qa.a: Yes — posture and movement assessment are part of how Dr. Brad evaluates patients, especially for chronic or recurring issues. Knowing how you actually move tells him more than a single snapshot.

qa.q: What is gait analysis?
qa.a: Gait analysis is the assessment of how you walk — looking for asymmetries, weakness, or compensations that may be contributing to pain or limiting performance. Dr. Brad uses this routinely, especially for foot, knee, hip, and low-back issues.

qa.q: Do you use any techniques besides manual adjustment?
qa.a: Yes — depending on the patient and the situation, Dr. Brad uses several techniques, including very gentle, low-force options for patients who prefer or need them. Tell him your preferences and he'll match the approach.

qa.q: What is the activator technique?
qa.a: The Activator is a small handheld instrument that delivers a quick, very gentle impulse to a joint. It's often used for patients who prefer or need a low-force approach, such as some seniors, very young patients, or anyone with osteoporosis.

qa.q: Do you do dry needling?
qa.a: Dry needling isn't currently part of our services. If you're interested in it specifically, call (540) 721-0044 and we can point you toward a provider who offers it.

qa.q: Do you do acupuncture?
qa.a: Acupuncture isn't part of our services. For acupuncture, we can suggest someone in the area — call us and we'll point you in the right direction.

qa.q: Do you sell supplements?
qa.a: We don't sell supplements. If you have nutrition questions related to your care, Dr. Brad is happy to discuss general guidance during your visit.

qa.q: What technique does Dr. Brad use most?
qa.a: Dr. Brad uses a range of manual techniques and adapts to the patient — full-spectrum hands-on chiropractic care, with gentler alternatives available when needed. There's no one signature technique he applies to everyone.

qa.q: Will I get heat or ice?
qa.a: Sometimes — heat or ice may be used in-office or recommended for home use depending on what's going on. As a general guideline, ice helps acute injuries (first 24–48 hours); heat is better for chronic muscle tension. Dr. Brad will tell you which to use.

qa.q: Can I just come in for a massage chair?
qa.a: The massage chairs are for our patients as part of their visits, not a stand-alone service. If you'd like to become a patient, give us a call at (540) 721-0044.

qa.q: Do you take insurance?
qa.a: We accept many major insurance plans. The simplest path is to call (540) 721-0044 with your card handy — we'll verify your specific plan and walk through what's covered before you come in.

qa.q: What insurance plans do you accept?
qa.a: We work with many of the major plans, but the specifics depend on the year and the plan. Call (540) 721-0044 with your insurance info and we'll confirm coverage for you specifically.

qa.q: Do you take Medicare?
qa.a: Medicare covers a portion of chiropractic care under specific circumstances. Call (540) 721-0044 with your Medicare info and we'll confirm what's covered for your situation.

qa.q: Do you take Medicaid?
qa.a: Medicaid chiropractic coverage varies. Call (540) 721-0044 with your card and we'll verify your specific situation.

qa.q: What if I don't have insurance?
qa.a: We see plenty of self-pay patients and our pricing is straightforward — no inflated rates because you're paying out of pocket. Call (540) 721-0044 and we'll talk through what your specific visit might cost.

qa.q: How much does a visit cost without insurance?
qa.a: Pricing depends on what's needed during the visit. Call (540) 721-0044 and we'll give you an honest estimate before you come in.

qa.q: Do you take HSA or FSA?
qa.a: Yes — chiropractic care is HSA- and FSA-eligible. Bring your HSA or FSA card and we'll process it like any other card.

qa.q: Do you offer payment plans?
qa.a: Talk to us — for longer care plans we'll work with you on something reasonable. Call (540) 721-0044 to talk it through.

qa.q: Do you accept credit cards?
qa.a: Yes — we accept Visa, Mastercard, and the usual major cards, plus HSA/FSA cards.

qa.q: Do you take auto insurance after an accident?
qa.a: Yes — we work with auto insurance and personal-injury cases. Call (540) 721-0044 and bring your claim info; we'll help walk you through it.

qa.q: Do you do workers' compensation?
qa.a: Yes — we work with workers' compensation cases. Call (540) 721-0044 with your claim information so we can confirm the process for your specific case.

qa.q: Do you have a new patient special?
qa.a: Pricing and any specials change. Call (540) 721-0044 and we'll tell you what's available right now.

qa.q: Do you offer family discounts?
qa.a: Family arrangements happen sometimes; the best path is to call (540) 721-0044 and tell us about your situation.

qa.q: How do insurance copays work?
qa.a: Your copay is the per-visit amount your insurance plan asks you to pay; it varies by plan. When you call (540) 721-0044 with your insurance info, we'll tell you your specific copay before your visit.

qa.q: Do you provide superbills?
qa.a: Yes — if your plan reimburses out-of-network chiropractic, we can provide a superbill you can submit to your insurance.

qa.q: I hurt my back wakeboarding — can you help?
qa.a: Yes — wakeboarding back injuries (often sudden twisting or a hard fall) are something we see regularly in the summer. Call (540) 721-0044 and we'll get you in. If you have severe pain, weakness, or numbness after a hard fall, head to an ER first.

qa.q: My shoulder is sore from waterskiing
qa.a: Waterskiing shoulder strain is a classic summer injury at the lake. Many patients do well with a combination of conservative care and a brief activity adjustment until the shoulder calms down. Call (540) 721-0044 to come in.

qa.q: I play pickleball and my shoulder hurts
qa.a: Pickleball shoulder is one of the most common things we see — particularly from overhead serves and slams. We work with a lot of lake pickleballers; usually some combination of care, technique adjustments, and shoulder-specific strengthening gets you back on court.

qa.q: My back hurts from boating all day
qa.a: Long boat days can be rough on the lower back — particularly with cold water exposure and engine vibration. Many patients do well with regular tune-ups during boating season plus a few specific exercises. Call (540) 721-0044 to schedule.

qa.q: My golf swing is bothering my back
qa.a: Yes — chronic golf-related back pain is something we see often. The mix of conservative care, swing-load awareness, and at-home rotational mobility work tends to keep patients playing the season.

qa.q: I'm retired and my back hurts more than it used to
qa.a: Very common — and we work with a lot of lake-area retirees on exactly this. Conservative care plus targeted strengthening and posture work often makes a real difference in day-to-day comfort. Call (540) 721-0044 to set up an exam.

qa.q: I tweaked my back on the dock
qa.a: Dock slips and lifts are some of our most common acute calls. If you have severe pain, numbness, or you can't bear weight, head to an ER. Otherwise, call (540) 721-0044 — early evaluation makes a difference.

qa.q: Should I get a tune-up before boating season?
qa.a: Many of our regulars do exactly that — a pre-season visit to address whatever's tightened up over the winter, plus a few exercises to prep for the demands of dock work, water activity, and longer days on your feet. Call (540) 721-0044 to schedule.

qa.q: I have a vacation home on the lake — can you treat me when I'm here?
qa.a: Absolutely — we work with many second-home patients who see us during their time at the lake. Call (540) 721-0044 ahead of your visits and we'll find times that fit your stay.

qa.q: I'm visiting Smith Mountain Lake — can I come in as a one-time patient?
qa.a: Yes — call (540) 721-0044 and we'll get you in. Visitors with sudden back or neck issues from boating, hiking, or travel are welcome.

qa.q: Chiropractor or physical therapist — which should I see?
qa.a: Chiropractors and physical therapists often share patients, with different emphases. Chiropractic centers on joint adjustment and conservative pain relief; PT centers on movement rehabilitation and exercise progression. For many issues, either is a reasonable first step. Dr. Brad will tell you honestly if PT is the better fit for your situation.

qa.q: Chiropractor or massage therapist — which do I need?
qa.a: Massage targets soft tissue — muscle tension, fascia, circulation. Chiropractic targets joint motion. They often pair well together; some patients use both for different reasons. Dr. Brad can talk through what makes sense for what you're experiencing.

qa.q: Should I see an orthopedist or a chiropractor first?
qa.a: For many non-emergency musculoskeletal issues, starting with conservative care like chiropractic is reasonable. Orthopedic referral usually comes in if imaging or surgical evaluation is needed. Dr. Brad will refer you out if that's the better path.

qa.q: Should I see my primary care doctor or a chiropractor for back pain?
qa.a: For most uncomplicated back pain, either is a reasonable starting point. If you have other symptoms — fever, weight loss, severe weakness, loss of bowel or bladder control — start with primary care or urgent care. Otherwise, conservative chiropractic care is often the first step.

qa.q: When should I go to the ER instead of a chiropractor?
qa.a: Go to the ER (or call 911) for: severe trauma, loss of consciousness, sudden numbness or weakness on one side, loss of bladder or bowel control, the worst headache of your life, chest pain or difficulty breathing, sudden vision changes, or any symptom that feels like a true emergency.

qa.q: Chiropractor or acupuncturist — which is right for me?
qa.a: They're different approaches and many patients use both for different reasons. Chiropractic centers on joint motion; acupuncture is part of traditional Chinese medicine. Dr. Brad is happy to talk through what makes sense for your situation.

qa.q: Chiropractic or pain management — which should I try?
qa.a: Pain management often involves medications, injections, or other procedures handled by a physician. Chiropractic is conservative, hands-on, non-pharmaceutical. For many patients, conservative care is the first step before considering pain management — Dr. Brad will give you an honest read.

qa.q: Chiropractor or sports medicine doc?
qa.a: Sports medicine physicians are MDs or DOs who specialize in athletic injuries and may handle injections, imaging, or surgery. Chiropractors handle conservative, hands-on care. Many active patients see both — Dr. Brad will refer you to a sports medicine physician if that's the right call.

qa.q: Chiropractor or osteopath (DO)?
qa.a: Osteopaths (DOs) are medical doctors with full prescribing and surgical training, who may also do manual techniques. Chiropractors (DCs) focus on joint and soft-tissue care without medication or surgery. Both are licensed; the right one depends on what you need.

qa.q: Why see Dr. Brad over another chiropractor?
qa.a: 25 years on Smith Mountain Lake; conservative-first philosophy without long-term contracts or upselling; patients regularly describe him as someone who explains the "why" behind every visit and gives at-home exercises so progress continues between visits. We'd rather earn your trust than make claims — call (540) 721-0044 and meet him.
